title: Access to Daylight and Views Improves Physical and Emotional Wellbeing of Office Workers: A Crossover Study
research_question: To investigate how two office environments, differing only in daylight conditions and window treatment (electrochromic glass vs. roller shades), impact occupants' environmental perceptions, physical health, and emotional wellbeing.

participants.description: Full-time office workers, average age 34 years (range: 23 to 55), 63% male, 37% female, predominantly White (53%), nearly all with college degree or higher (90%). Study conducted in Durham, North Carolina.
participants.recruitment: Not explicitly stated, but implies recruitment for the overarching EVOLV Study.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Two identical West-facing office environments (size, orientation, layout, furniture, HVAC, overhead and task lighting) differing only in window treatment. One office had dynamic electrochromic (EC) glass windows, which tint based on solar conditions (58% to 0.5% visible transmittance). The other office had functionally standard windows (58% visible transmittance glass) occluded by fixed 1.5% visible transmittance fabric roller shades at 75% window area occlusion.

measures.instrument: Binary (yes/no) for 'space feeling too dim', 'space feeling too bright', 'lack of daylight', 'overabundance of daylight', 'undesirable color of lighting', 'glare reflected off computer screens/surfaces'
Binary (yes/no) for 'tired or strained eyes', 'headache', 'difficulty remembering things or concentrating', 'unusual fatigue', 'tension or irritability'
PANAS questionnaire (10 items, 5-point Likert scale, sum 10-50)

findings.mechanism: Improved daylight and views contribute to a more positive emotional state.

findings.antecedent: Office condition (EC Glass vs. Roller Shades)
findings.mechanism: Optimized daylight and views positively influence mood and reduce feelings of depression.

mechanisms: Windows control daylight and provide connection to the outside, impacting physical and mental health.
Daylight qualities (intensity, spectra, timing) drive circadian-effective lighting via non-visual pathways, influencing sleep and metabolism.
Daylight and views shape perceptions of indoor environmental quality, impacting visual comfort and reducing eyestrain by providing long-distance views for eye muscle relaxation.
Excessive daylight and glare can cause eyestrain and Computer Vision Syndrome; optimal lighting conditions are crucial.
Daylight and views impart psychological and mental health benefits by reducing stress and improving workplace satisfaction, and influencing serotonin levels (Seasonal Affective Disorder).
Electrochromic (EC) glazing dynamically tints based on solar conditions, maintaining maximal access to circadian-effective daylight, glare mitigation, and consistent views.

The benefits to emotional affect from working in the EC Glass office are comparable to those from active behavioral interventions like yoga and meditation, suggesting a strong environmental influence on mood.
moderators: Participant proximity to the window (5-10 feet vs. 15-20 feet away)
implementation_implications: Optimizing daylight and access to views in office environments benefits environmental satisfaction, physical health (reduced eyestrain), and emotional wellbeing (improved affect, reduced depression).
Electrochromic glass is a healthy building design element that improves occupant health and performance, beyond just energy efficiency.

Designing spaces that promote physical and mental health through daylighting strategies is important for building owners, architects, and tenants to support people's health and organizational success.
A physical workplace environment that fails to optimize for employee health can be costly due to illness-related absenteeism and reduced cognitive performance from depression.

limitations: Subjective and self-report nature of many outcomes, leading to potential response bias.
Participants were not explicitly made aware of study objectives, but were not blinded to test conditions as the difference in window treatment was visually apparent.
Small sample size (N=30) for office workers, though crossover design and repeated measures provided statistical power.
Limited detailed knowledge and environmental measurements of participants' baseline (Weeks 1 and 4) environments.

paper_metadata.title: Access to Daylight and Views Improves Physical and Emotional Wellbeing of Office Workers: A Crossover Study
paper_metadata.crossref_title: Access to Daylight and Views Improves Physical and Emotional Wellbeing of Office Workers: A Crossover Study
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: While buildings are designed with expansive windows to allow for abundant daylight and views, in practice, they are frequently occluded to control for heat and glare. Electrochromic glass windows are a solution designed to maximize occupant access to daylight and views throughout the day, and previous research has demonstrated the benefits they can impart on sleep and cognition. We extend this research to quantify its impacts on the perceived physical and emotional wellbeing of occupants in an office environment. 30 office workers spent 5 days working in each of two West-facing offices that were identical with the exception of the window treatment: one with dynamic electrochromic windows and the other with functionally standard windows partially occluded by a fixed roller shade. When working in the office with electrochromic glass, participants were 8-fold more likely of report satisfaction with daylight conditions and 6.5-fold more likely to report satisfaction with views of the outside, were 48% less likely to report eyestrain, perceived a significant benefit to positive affect and were 77% less likely to report feeling depressed. This study adds to the growing body of research demonstrating the importance of daylighting strategies in designing spaces that support the physical and mental health of occupants.
